transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?

Well, thanks for seeing me. Honestly, I keep forgetting my appointments and daily health stuff, even when I really try to stay on top of it. It's getting pretty frustrating because I know how important it all is, but I just can't seem to keep track of it lately.
Did these attention and memory problems start only after a head injury, illness, or other medical problem, or have you had them since childhood?

To be honest, these tendencies go all the way back to when I was a kid. Back in grade school, teachers were always sending notes home because I wouldn't stay in my seat, talked over everyone, and got in trouble for roaming the classroom. It's just gotten much harder to manage recently with all these new health routines.
Did these attention and restlessness problems continue across school, home, and work or daily life as you grew up, causing problems in more than one setting?

Yes, they've definitely followed me throughout my life and affect me in multiple places. Right now, it's not just causing problems with my medical routines at home, but I'm also letting people down at the senior center when I miss commitments or can't stick to the tasks they're counting on me for.
Do you still often have trouble staying focused, sitting still, or acting before thinking, even now as an adult?

Oh, absolutely, I still struggle with all of that every single day. I constantly feel restless, like there's a motor running inside me, which makes me fidget, pace, and struggle to sit still during appointments. My mind is always drifting off to other things, and I constantly catch myself interrupting people or jumping ahead before they can even finish their sentences.
Do you also often lose things, make careless mistakes, or have trouble finishing tasks because you get distracted, even when the task is important?

Yes, I really struggle to finish tasks because I get so easily distracted. For instance, I'll sit down to write my daily blood pressure numbers, but then a bird outside the window or a joke from game night catches my attention, and I wander off before ever writing them down.
As a child, were you mainly inattentive and forgetful, or were you also very hyperactive and impulsive, such as constantly running/climbing, blurting out answers, or having trouble waiting your turn?

Oh, I was definitely very hyperactive and impulsive back then. Teachers were constantly sending notes home because I wouldn't stay in my seat, talked over everyone, and got in trouble for blurting things out and roaming the classroom instead of doing my work quietly.
Before age 12, were your symptoms mainly inattentive, mainly hyperactive/impulsive, or clearly both?

I was definitely mainly hyperactive and impulsive back then. My teachers were always sending notes home because I couldn't stay in my seat, talked over everyone, and got in trouble for blurting things out and roaming the classroom instead of doing my work quietly.
Before age 15, did you also have repeated behavior problems like fighting, bullying, stealing, lying, destroying property, or serious rule-breaking?

No, I never really had those kinds of severe behavior problems like fighting, stealing, or destroying property. I was just a very hyperactive, loud kid who couldn't sit still, but I wasn't destructive or mean.
Do you also have trouble sleeping because your mind feels too active, or are you usually able to sleep normally when you want to?
No, I haven't really noticed any major trouble with my sleep. Once I actually get into bed, I usually sleep pretty well.

final_diagnosis.reason: The interview confirms a lifelong pattern of inattention, hyperactivity, and impulsivity beginning in childhood, present across multiple settings, and persisting into adulthood with current functional impairment (missed appointments, difficulty completing health routines, problems at the senior center). Symptoms clearly began before age 12 and are not better explained by a head injury, sleep disorder, or conduct disorder.
